findings.title: Missing SameSite cookie attribute in default configuration
findings.evidence: Default configuration at line 40 of .defaults.yml has `sameSite:` commented out (not set). When cfg.Cfg.Cookie.SameSite is empty string, the SameSite() function in cookie.go returns http.SameSite(0), which means no SameSite attribute is set on session cookies.
findings.impact: Session cookies without SameSite attribute are vulnerable to cross-site request forgery (CSRF) attacks where an attacker can trick a user into making requests from another site that will include the session cookie. The impact is that an authenticated user visiting a malicious site could have their session used to perform actions without their knowledge.
findings.preconditions: User must be authenticated to Vouch Proxy and visiting a site controlled by an attacker while the legitimate Vouch Proxy site is open in another tab or window.
findings.recommendation: Set a default SameSite mode in .defaults.yml. SameSiteLaxMode is recommended as it allows same-site requests while blocking cross-site requests. Add to .defaults.yml: 'sameSite: Lax' (line 40). Users can override this in their configuration as needed. Modern browsers (Chrome 51+, Firefox 60+, Safari 13+) support this attribute.
findings.inference: While HttpOnly=true and Secure=true are set by default (preventing JavaScript access and requiring HTTPS), the lack of SameSite means the cookie is still sent in cross-site requests. The vulnerability exists unless users explicitly configure SameSite in their config.yml.
findings.what_would_settle_it: Verification that all default configuration files and documentation recommend SameSite configuration, and that new deployments follow this guidance in their config examples.

triage.reason: No compensating control is evident. HttpOnly and Secure help but don't prevent CSRF from cross-site requests that don't require JavaScript access.
The SameSite attribute is not attacker-controlled; it's a server-side setting.
The sink is the browser's cookie handling, which does implement CSRF attacks when SameSite is not set.
This is default configuration that ships in production. .defaults.yml is loaded by Configure() in main.go for all deployments.
The cookie behavior is not intended to be vulnerable; SameSite should be set but isn't by default.
This is a code-based configuration issue, not external to the repository.
The SameSite attribute is exactly what it looks like - missing - not a different construct.
This is a load-bearing defense; there is no secondary mitigation that makes the cookie CSRF-safe once HttpOnly is set.

findings.limits: This finding is classified as `probable` rather than `confirmed` because: (1) the actual CSRF impact depends on the specific deployment context and how users have configured their systems; (2) users may mitigate this by configuring SameSite in their own config.yml; (3) the Nginx auth_request module context may provide additional protections depending on how it's deployed.

ruled_out.where: generateStateNonce() in handlers/login.go uses securerandom.URLBase64InBytes(base64Bytes) where base64Bytes=32, providing 256 bits of entropy which is cryptographically secure

getValidRequestedURL() in handlers/login.go validates: (1) scheme is http/https, (2) hostname matches configured domains or cookie domain, (3) query parameters don't contain dangerous strings, (4) cookie secure flag matches scheme
LogoutHandler in handlers/logout.go validates redirectURL against cfg.Cfg.LogoutRedirectURLs allowlist (line 61-67) before any redirect

ruled_out.class: JWT token algorithm substitution (alg:none, algorithm confusion)
ruled_out.where: ParseTokenString in pkg/jwtmanager/jwtmanager.go validates token.Method == jwt.GetSigningMethod(cfg.Cfg.JWT.SigningMethod) at line 152, preventing algorithm attacks

ruled_out.class: JWT signature bypass with empty key
ruled_out.where: Configuration validation in pkg/cfg/cfg.go ensures JWT.Secret is at least minBase64Length (44 chars) for HMAC signing methods (line 432-436)

Cookie.ClearCookie() is called in LoginHandler (line 41) before session creation, and session path is restricted to /auth/{state}/ (line 58), but verified regeneration on login was not traced through full test execution
Gorilla CookieStore is initialized with cfg.Cfg.Session.Key (handlers/handlers.go:59) which is either user-configured or auto-generated with 32 random bytes (pkg/cfg/cfg.go:361-367)

Error messages in handlers do not distinguish 'user not found' from 'wrong password' at the authentication layer, but user verification happens post-OAuth so IdP determines enumeration surface (not audited against remote IdP behavior)

ruled_out.where: ValidateRequestHandler validates r.Host against jwt claims.Audience AND against domains.Matches(r.Host), requiring match on both (handlers/validate.go:55)
